nodes.name: Extract Email Fields
nodes.notes: Normalises the Gmail Trigger output into the five standard fields the pipeline expects: subject, from_name, from_email, body, received_at. Handles Gmail's object-based 'from' field format ({address, name}) and sanitises the email body by stripping newlines, tabs, and control characters that would break downstream JSON templates.

parameters.jsonBody:
={
  "model": "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Read the email below and classify it into exactly ONE of these three paths.

Do NOT route based on keywords in the subject line alone. Read the full email body carefully before deciding.

'k' - A business or organisation inquiring about AI consulting, CRM intelligence, data platform services, business transformation, or professional services. The sender wants to BUY Acme AI's consulting or AI services. This applies to companies from ANY industry — retail, SaaS, finance, healthcare, manufacturing — as long as they want AI or consulting services.

'consumer' - An individual person inquiring about buying furniture or home products for personal use at their home address. They are asking about specific products, prices, stock, or delivery.

'retail' - A business owner or retailer inquiring SPECIFICALLY about wholesale furniture purchasing, bulk orders, minimum order quantities, trade pricing, or stocking furniture products in their store to resell.

CRITICAL RULES:
- If the email mentions AI, CRM, data platform, digital transformation, or consulting services = always 'k', regardless of what industry the sender works in.
- A retail company or retail chain wanting AI or consulting services = 'k', NOT 'retail'.
- 'retail' is ONLY for businesses wanting to buy furniture wholesale to stock in their store.
- When in doubt between 'k' and 'retail' = choose 'k'.

Return ONLY one of these exact values: k, consumer, retail
No explanation. No markdown. Just the single word.

Email subject: {{$json.subject}}
Sender email: {{$json.from_email}}
Email body: {{$json.body}}"
    }
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 10,
  "seed": 0,
  "top_p": 1
}

nodes.name: Detect Path
nodes.notes: Calls Cerebras LLM to classify the email into one of three paths: 'k' (Acme AI B2B professional services), 'consumer' (Lumen Living individual furniture buyer), or 'retail' (Lumen Living wholesale/retail partner). Returns a single word classification used by the Route by Path switch node.

nodes.name: Parse Path
nodes.notes: Parses the LLM classification response and extracts the path value (k, consumer, or retail). Falls back to 'k' if the response is invalid. Also carries forward the original email fields (subject, from_name, from_email, body, received_at) for the downstream extraction nodes.

nodes.name: Route by Path
nodes.notes: Switch node that routes the lead to the correct LLM extraction prompt based on the classified path. Output 0 = K (Acme AI B2B), Output 1 = Consumer (Lumen Living individual), Output 2 = Retail (Lumen Living wholesale). Each path has its own field extraction prompt tailored to that business context.

parameters.jsonBody:
={
  "model": "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "You are a CRM lead qualification assistant for Acme AI, an Australian B2B AI consulting firm. All clients are based in Australia or dealing in Australian dollars unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Read the email below and extract structured lead information.

Return ONLY valid JSON with this exact structure:
{
  "sender_name": "",
  "sender_email": "",
  "company_name": "",
  "team_size": "",
  "stated_revenue_aud": "",
  "sector_fit_signal": "",
  "sector_fit_confidence": "",
  "exec_sponsor_signal": "",
  "ai_appetite_signal": "",
  "budget_timeline_signal": "",
  "relationship_signal": "",
  "budget_signal": "",
  "timeline_signal": "",
  "price_shopping": false,
  "cannot_influence": false,
  "fields_inferred": 0
}

---

- sender_name: full name of the person writing. Empty string if not found.

- sender_email: email address of the sender. Empty string if not found.

- company_name: exact company name if explicitly mentioned. Empty string if not found. Do not infer from email domain.

- team_size: a number only if explicitly mentioned. Empty string if not found.

- stated_revenue_aud: company annual revenue or turnover as a full integer in AUD only if explicitly stated. Examples: 80000000 for $80M, 90000000 for $90M ARR. If given in EUR multiply by 1.65. If given in GBP multiply by 1.95. Empty string if not mentioned.
  HARD RULES:
  - Acme AI is an Australian firm. Any dollar sign '$' = Australian dollars (AUD) by default. Never assume USD unless the email explicitly says 'USD', 'US dollars', or 'US$'.
  - stated_revenue_aud is the company ANNUAL REVENUE or TURNOVER only. Never use a project budget, initiative budget, or allocated spend figure as revenue.
  - If the email contains both a revenue figure and a budget figure, always use the revenue or turnover figure here and ignore the budget figure entirely.
  - ALL ARR figures are Australian dollars (AUD) unless the email explicitly states USD, EUR, or GBP.
  - '$90M ARR' = 90000000. '$150M ARR' = 150000000. Never multiply by 1.55 unless USD is stated.
  - Only convert to AUD if the email explicitly says 'USD' (x1.55), 'EUR' or 'euros' (x1.65), 'GBP' or 'pounds' (x1.95).

---

- sector_fit_signal: classify the company PRIMARY industry into exactly one of: core, adjacent, problem_match, no_fit.

  'core' = Organisation's primary business activity matches one of the following ANZSIC Divisions, each confirmed by at least one named Acme AI client.
  Division O — Public Administration and Safety: government department, statutory body, local council, regulatory authority, policy body, utilities. Named clients: Australian Government departments, NSW/VIC/QLD departments, Austrade, VLRC, AIMS, Water NSW, CenITex, Fraser Coast, Northern Beaches, Macedon Ranges.
  Division K — Financial and Insurance Services: bank, superannuation fund, insurance company, investment manager, credit union, mortgage lender, infrastructure investment fund. Named clients: ANZ, ASFA, ATC Insurance, Avant Insurance, Community First Credit Union, Defence Bank, Hunter Hall, Plenary, RAMS.
  Division P — Education and Training: university, college, school, vocational institute, admissions body, pathway education provider, specialist education. Named clients: ACU, RMIT, La Trobe, Federation University, Monash College, VTAC, William Angliss, Lycée Condorcet, Autism Teaching Institute.
  Division M — Professional Scientific and Technical Services: law firm, consulting firm, compliance provider, training and compliance, recruitment agency. Named clients: MinterEllison, Archway Group, CompliSpace, Safetycare, Drake International.
  Division H — Accommodation and Food Services: luxury hotel, hotel group, resort, ski resort, destination management, restaurant. Named clients: InterContinental Sydney, Holiday Inn, Lancemore Group, TFE Hotels, Falls Creek Resort, Ducks Nuts.
  Division R — Arts and Recreation Services: contemporary art institution, national sporting body, state sporting body, publisher, media production. Named clients: Australian Centre for Contemporary Art, Surfing Australia, Surfing NSW.
  Division Q — Health Care and Social Assistance: social services organisation, veterans support body, charity, not-for-profit social services. Named clients: Berry Street, Relationships Australia, Adopt Change, Legacy Australia.
  Division S — Other Services / Not-for-Profit: religious organisation, community services, veterans support. Named clients: Anglican Church General Synod, Legacy Australia.
  Division N — Administrative and Support Services: business events, convention bureau, ticketing service, venue management, events company. Named clients: Business Events Sydney, Playbill, Sydney Showground.
  Division I — Transport Postal and Warehousing: public transport operator. Named clients: Yarra Trams.
  Division J — Information Media and Telecommunications: publisher, media company, media production, broadcasting. Named clients: News Corp, Art Edited, Magnesium Media.

  'adjacent' = Industry is different but close enough that Acme AI's core methodology transfers with minor adaptation.
  Division G — Retail Trade: retail chain, homewares retailer, apparel brand, action sports brand, liquor retail. Named clients: Globe International, Sheridan Australia, Liquor Marketing Group.
  Division L — Rental Hiring and Real Estate Services: property management firm, student accommodation provider, real estate agency. Named clients: Campus Living Villages, Goodman Property Services.
  Division C — Manufacturing (agrichemical and crop science ONLY): agrichemical company, crop science company. Named client: Nufarm Australia. All other manufacturing = NO FIT.
  Division A — Agriculture Forestry and Fishing (agrichemical only): agrichemical, crop science. Primary farming and livestock = NO FIT.
  Division B — Mining (industry body and advocacy ONLY): mining advocacy body, industry association for mining. Named client: Minerals Council of Australia. Mining operations themselves = NO FIT.
  Technology / SaaS platforms: SaaS company, HR tech, property tech, sports tech platform. Named clients: Livehire, PEXA, GolfSpace.
  Consumer Goods: FMCG company, hospitality products supplier, consumer goods brand. Named clients: Nestle Australia, Vanity Group.

  'problem_match' = Sector is outside core AND adjacent BUT the email explicitly states a problem that maps onto a Acme AI service. Accept ONLY if one of the following is explicitly stated — do not infer: we need an AI platform, we are building an AI solution, we need a CRM or our CRM is not working, we need a knowledge management system, we have data we do not know how to use, we need AI governance, we need a data infrastructure or data platform.

  'no_fit' = Industry would require Acme AI to redesign its offering from scratch. No problem overlap.
  Includes: heavy manufacturing (coatings, industrial, wool processing), mining operations, construction, electricity/gas/waste, wholesale trade, primary agriculture/livestock.
  Important: if sector is unclear or not stated, assign no_fit and set sector_fit_confidence to inferred.

  RULES:
  - Never assign core based on problem statement alone — sector must match first.
  - When choosing between two levels always go LOWER not higher.
  - A luxury hotel or hotel group = core (Division H). A small cafe or restaurant with no hotel group context = no_fit.
  - Only use problem_match if sector is outside BOTH core AND adjacent AND the problem is explicitly stated.

---

- sector_fit_confidence: exactly one of:
  'stated' = The lead explicitly stated their industry or business type in the email. ANZSIC division confirmed directly from their words.
  'inferred' = The lead did NOT explicitly state their industry. AI had to infer from company name, email domain, or context. If inferred, increment fields_inferred by 1 even if all other 5 attributes are fully stated.

---

- exec_sponsor_signal: exactly one of: named_mandate, engaged_no_mandate, will_find, none.

  'named_mandate' = A named executive sponsor is confirmed. Rep can state their name and title. They have budget authority and are actively driving the initiative. The SENDER must be the sponsor themselves — proxy contacts cannot be named_mandate.
  Signal words: our CTO is driving this, the CEO wants to, our CDO has signed off, the board has approved, X is sponsoring this project.

  'engaged_no_mandate' = A senior contact is engaged and interested but has not yet secured formal sign-off or budget authority. Also use when the sender is a proxy reaching out on behalf of a named person driving the initiative.
  Signal words: I'm pushing for this internally, I want to get this approved, I'm trying to get budget for this.

  'will_find' = No sponsor identified yet AND the contact explicitly says they will find one or escalate to a decision maker.
  Signal words: I need to find the right person to own this, I'll speak to my manager, I'm not sure who would own this, I have not been able to get sign-off yet, I am hoping to build the business case.

  'none' = No internal owner exists and the contact gives no indication of finding one. Contact is simply curious or exploring with no organisational backing and no plan to escalate.
  Signal words: just curious, wanted to explore, not sure if this is right for us, just checking, no mention of any internal stakeholder at all.

  RULES:
  - named_mandate requires ALL THREE: named person + confirmed budget authority + actively driving. Missing any one = not named_mandate.
  - Proxy sender = engaged_no_mandate at most. Never named_mandate.
  - 'I have not been able to get sign-off yet' or 'I am hoping to build the business case' = will_find.
  - No mention of any internal stakeholder, decision maker, manager, or sponsor at all = none.
  - When in doubt always go LOWER not higher.

---

- ai_appetite_signal: exactly one of: mandate_approved, mandate_pending, personal_initiative, curiosity. Empty string if no AI mention at all.

  'mandate_approved' = Organisation has made a formal decision to invest in AI AND budget approved by finance or board. Both mandate and funding exist.
  Signal words: we have an approved AI budget, the board has approved, we've allocated funds, we have a mandate to move forward with AI.

  'mandate_pending' = Leadership has decided to invest in AI but budget is still moving through finance approval.
  Signal words: we're waiting for budget approval, the initiative has been agreed but not yet funded.

  'personal_initiative' = The contact personally wants to pursue AI but has not taken it to leadership or secured organisational backing.
  Signal words: I personally think we should do this, I've been trying to get this off the ground, I'm exploring this on my own, I have been pushing for this but have not got sign-off.

  'curiosity' = Organisation is exploring AI but has no investment plan, no timeline, no concrete next step.
  Signal words: we've been thinking about AI, we're curious about what's possible, not sure if AI is right for us, just exploring.

  RULES:
  - Never return empty if any AI mention exists — minimum is curiosity.
  - mandate_approved requires BOTH: formal decision confirmed AND budget approved by finance or board.

---

- budget_timeline_signal: exactly one of: both_clear, one_clear, both_approximate, neither.

  'both_clear' = Lead can state an approximate budget range AND a target decision quarter. Both confirmed.
  Signal words: we have roughly X budget, we want to decide by Q3, our timeline is six months.

  'one_clear' = One confirmed clearly; the other is approximate but plausible.
  Signal words: we have some budget but haven't finalised the amount, we want to start soon but haven't set a date.

  'both_approximate' = Lead gives rough ranges for BOTH budget AND timeline — neither confirmed but both positively stated.
  Signal words: probably around X, maybe next year, sometime in the first half, we're thinking roughly X budget.

  'neither' = Lead cannot state any budget range or any timeline. No internal conversations have happened.
  Signal words: no budget in mind, no particular timeline, don't have a budget, not sure of the timeline.

  RULES:
  - 'I do not have a budget and no particular timeline' = neither. No exceptions.
  - 'I don't have a budget in mind' = neither.
  - Any sentence with 'don't have', 'not sure', 'no budget', 'no timeline', 'haven't confirmed' = neither unless a specific number or quarter is also explicitly stated.
  - Wanting to 'start a conversation' or 'have an introductory call' is NOT a budget or timeline signal = neither.
  - both_approximate requires BOTH budget AND timeline to be positively stated as rough ranges.
  - When in doubt always go LOWER not higher.

---

- relationship_signal: exactly one of: trusted_intro, general_intro, event_met, cold. Empty string if cannot be determined.

  'trusted_intro' = Lead introduced by a confirmed existing Acme AI client, partner, or close colleague. Email must explicitly state the referrer is an existing Acme AI client or has worked with Acme AI.
  Signal words: referred by X who is your client, X who worked with you suggested I reach out.

  'general_intro' = Lead introduced by someone known to Acme AI but not confirmed as an existing client.
  Signal words: X suggested I contact you, I got your name from X, someone mentioned you.

  'event_met' = Lead met Acme AI at a conference, webinar, or industry event.
  Signal words: we met at, I saw your talk at, I attended your webinar, I spoke to you at the summit.

  'cold' = No prior relationship. Found Acme AI online, LinkedIn, website.
  Signal words: found your website, came across on LinkedIn, saw your post online.

  RULES:
  - 'X suggested I contact you' alone = general_intro. Never trusted_intro unless email explicitly says X is an existing Acme AI client.
  - 'Found your website online' or 'came across on LinkedIn' = cold.

---

- budget_signal: exact number or range if explicitly stated. Empty string if vague or missing.
- timeline_signal: exact timeframe if explicitly stated. Empty string if vague or missing.
- price_shopping: true if comparing costs across vendors with price-only questions. false otherwise.
- cannot_influence: true if contact confirmed they cannot reach or influence the final decision maker. false otherwise.
- fields_inferred: count of how many of these 6 attributes you had to INFER because the information was COMPLETELY ABSENT from the email — sector_fit_signal, exec_sponsor_signal, ai_appetite_signal, budget_timeline_signal, relationship_signal, stated_revenue_aud. Also increment by 1 if sector_fit_confidence = inferred even if all other 5 are fully stated. Return 0 to 6.

---

GENERAL RULES:
- Return only the JSON object. No markdown. No explanations.
- Only use values from the controlled vocabulary listed above.
- Conservative classification always. When choosing between two levels pick the lower one.
- Never upgrade a classification based on assumptions.
- Use signal words as guides but paraphrased equivalents count.

Email subject: {{$json.subject}}
Sender name: {{$json.from_name}}
Sender email: {{$json.from_email}}
Email body: {{$json.body}}"
    }
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 600,
  "seed": 0,
  "top_p": 1
}

nodes.name: LLM Extract K
nodes.notes: Calls Cerebras LLM with the Acme AI B2B extraction prompt. Extracts structured fields from the email: sender_name, sender_email, company_name, team_size, stated_revenue_aud, sector_fit_signal, exec_sponsor_signal, ai_appetite_signal, budget_timeline_signal, relationship_signal, budget_signal, timeline_signal, price_shopping, cannot_influence_decision, fields_inferred. Uses controlled vocabulary with conservative defaults.

parameters.jsonBody:
={
  "model": "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "You are a CRM lead extraction assistant for Lumen Living, a luxury Vietnamese furniture brand.

Read the customer message below and extract structured information.

Return ONLY valid JSON with this exact structure — no markdown, no explanation:
{
  "sender_name": "",
  "sender_email": "",
  "sender_phone": "",
  "extracted_city": "",
  "extracted_district": "",
  "product_category": "",
  "purchase_intent_signal": "",
  "product_fit_signal": "",
  "buyer_urgency_signal": "",
  "source_channel_signal": "",
  "designer_flag": false,
  "price_shopping": false,
  "is_custom": false
}

---

- sender_name: full name of the person sending the message. Empty string if not provided.
- sender_email: email address of the sender. Empty string if not provided.
- sender_phone: phone number of the sender. Empty string if not provided.
- extracted_city: city the customer is based in or wants delivery to. Empty string if not mentioned.
- extracted_district: district within the city. Empty string if not mentioned.

- product_category: the specific product the customer is asking about. Use the product name if mentioned (e.g. 'Oslo dining set', 'Stilt Sofa'). If they ask about a general category use that (e.g. 'sofa', 'dining table', 'bed'). Empty string if no product mentioned.

---

- purchase_intent_signal: classify the customer's buying intent into exactly one of: direct_intent, high_interest, passive_interest, no_signal.

  'direct_intent' = asking about price, availability, ordering, delivery, or payment. Ready to buy or very close.
  Signal words: how much, price, cost, order, buy, purchase, available, delivery, payment, can I get, want to buy.

  'high_interest' = strong interest but not yet asking about price or ordering. Asking for photos, dimensions, collections, styles, options.
  Signal words: interested in, love your, can you show, what collections, do you have, looking for, photos, dimensions.

  'passive_interest' = casual browsing with no clear intent. Just looking, for future reference, someday.
  Signal words: just looking, no rush, someday, future reference, browsing, curious.

  'no_signal' = cannot determine any intent from the message.

  RULES:
  - Default to 'high_interest' for ambiguous cases.
  - A customer asking for photos, dimensions, or product details = high_interest not passive_interest.

---

- product_fit_signal: classify how well the requested product fits Lumen Living's range into exactly one of: similar, custom_order, unavailable.

  Lumen Living sells: sofas, armchairs, dining tables, dining chairs, beds, bed frames, sideboards, shelving, coffee tables, side tables, foosball tables, chess sets, outdoor furniture, home decor accessories.

  'similar' = product is in or close to Lumen Living's range. Default for all furniture and home decor enquiries.
  'custom_order' = customer is asking for a custom size, colour, or modification.
  Signal words: custom, bespoke, made to measure, specific size, can you make.
  'unavailable' = product is completely outside Lumen Living's range. Must be unambiguous — electronics, clothing, food, appliances, automotive only.

  RULES:
  - Default to 'similar' for all furniture and home decor enquiries.
  - Only use 'unavailable' if the product is clearly and unambiguously outside the range.
  - If no product is mentioned, return 'similar'.

---

- buyer_urgency_signal: classify into exactly one of: immediate, normal, unknown.

  'immediate' = Customer explicitly states a deadline, project timeline, or same-day need.
  Signal words: urgent, ASAP, this week, need today, 3D model, client is waiting, presentation tomorrow, confirmed price, confirmed lead time, won't include unless confirmed, substitute something else.
  
  'normal' = No urgency language detected but message contains at least one of the following: customer names a specific product, asks about price, asks about stock or availability, asks about delivery. Active interest present but no time pressure. Standard buying behaviour with no time pressure.
  
  'unknown' = No urgency language and no buying signal present. Message is exploratory, passive, too short to classify, or in an unsupported language. Do not penalise — default to normal routing.

  RULES:
  - Default to 'normal' for most enquiries.
  - Only use 'unknown' if message is genuinely too short or ambiguous.

---

- source_channel_signal: classify how the customer found Lumen Living into exactly one of: paid_ad_click, direct_message, organic_comment, cold_unknown.

  Choose only ONE. Never combine. If signals for more than one are present, pick the strongest — the order below is strongest to weakest.

  'paid_ad_click' = customer references an ad, sponsored post, or promotion.
  Signal words: saw your ad, clicked your ad, sponsored post, your promotion, shop now, ad came up on my feed.
  Do NOT choose this if they only say they 'saw' the product without referencing an ad or promotion specifically.

  'direct_message' = customer sought the store out themselves, with no ad or post prompting them.
  Signal words: found your page, found your website, looked you up, searched for furniture, came across your page, sent you a message, DM.

  'organic_comment' = customer references seeing a post, story, or tagged content — but no ad.
  Signal words: saw your post, saw your Instagram, saw your Facebook, saw your story, someone tagged you, I follow your page.

  'cold_unknown' = no reference at all to how they found the store. No ad, post, search, or referral mentioned. Default to this when no channel signal is present. Do not infer a higher bucket without explicit evidence.

---

- designer_flag: true if the customer identifies themselves as an interior designer, architect, or trade professional. false otherwise.
  Signal words: interior designer, architect, trade account, professional discount, I design for clients, FF&E consultant, 3D model, client project, for my client, specification.

- price_shopping: true if the customer is explicitly comparing prices across multiple stores or asking which store is cheapest.
  Look for: mentioning they checked or visited other stores, asking which is cheapest, comparing your price to another store, saying another store offers it cheaper.
  Examples: 'I also checked IKEA', 'comparing prices between stores', 'another store has it for less', 'which is the cheapest option'.
  false if they are only asking about your price without comparing to other stores.

- is_custom: true if the customer is asking for a custom size, colour, material, or modification. false otherwise.

---

GENERAL RULES:
- Return only the JSON object. No markdown. No explanations.
- Preserve all names, numbers, and addresses exactly as they appear.
- Default conservatively — go lower when signals are ambiguous.

Customer message:
Subject: {{$json.subject}}
Body: {{$json.body}}"
    }
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 400,
  "seed": 0,
  "top_p": 1
}

nodes.notes: Calls Cerebras LLM with the Lumen Living consumer extraction prompt. Extracts: sender_name, sender_email, product_requested, purchase_intent_signal, location_signal, product_fit_signal, source_channel_signal, contact_completeness_signal, fields_inferred. Tailored to individual furniture buyers in Ho Chi Minh City.

parameters.jsonBody:
={
  "model": "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "You are a lead qualification assistant for Lumen Living, a luxury furniture brand in Vietnam.

Read the business inquiry below and extract structured lead information.

Return ONLY valid JSON with this exact structure — no markdown, no explanation:
{
  "sender_name": "",
  "sender_email": "",
  "sender_phone": "",
  "company_name": "",
  "store_count": null,
  "extracted_city": "",
  "extracted_district": "",
  "wholesale_intent_signal": "",
  "business_legitimacy_signal": "",
  "order_volume_signal": "",
  "product_range_signal": "",
  "relationship_source_signal": "",
  "price_shopping": false
}

---

- sender_name: full name of the person writing. Empty string if not found.
- sender_email: email address if present. Empty string if not found.
- sender_phone: phone number if present. Empty string if not found.
- company_name: exact proper business name if explicitly mentioned. Empty string if not found. Do not infer from email domain. A description like 'a home goods store' or 'my shop' is NOT a company name.
- store_count: number of store locations if explicitly stated as an integer. null if not mentioned.
- extracted_city: city or province name mentioned. Empty string if not found.
- extracted_district: district name or number if mentioned. Empty string if not found.

---

- wholesale_intent_signal: classify into exactly one of: explicit_wholesale, moq_volume, range_inquiry, no_b2b_signal.

  'explicit_wholesale' = Retailer explicitly asks about wholesale pricing, trade accounts, MOQ, margin structure, distributor agreements, or trade terms. Clearest possible B2B buying language.
  Signal words: wholesale price, trade account, trade terms, margin, reseller, distributor, can we open an account, payment terms.

  'moq_volume' = Retailer asks about minimum order quantity, volume discounts, or bulk pricing without explicitly mentioning trade terms.
  Signal words: MOQ, minimum order, how many units, volume discount, bulk order, bulk price, large quantity.

  'range_inquiry' = Retailer asks about the product catalogue, styles, or range broadly, OR expresses intent to stock or carry the products without asking about wholesale pricing or trade terms. Stocking interest or exploration — not a trade-pricing question.
  Signal words: what products do you carry, catalogue, what styles, collections, interested in stocking, want to carry your range, looking to add your products, just exploring, thinking about, for the future.

  'no_b2b_signal' = No wholesale language at all. Message reads as a standard retail inquiry about a single item for personal use. Fires TP7 to re-route to the consumer path.

  RULES:
  - explicit_wholesale requires explicit mention of wholesale pricing, MOQ, margin, trade terms, or a trade account.
  - A retailer who says they want to stock or carry your products but does NOT ask about trade pricing = range_inquiry, not explicit_wholesale.
  - When in doubt go LOWER not higher.

---

- business_legitimacy_signal: classify into exactly one of: full_identity, name_address_only, unverified_claim, no_identity.

  'full_identity' = Proper business name + physical store address (or registration) + personal contact (email or phone). All three present.
  'name_address_only' = Proper business name AND address present, but the contact given appears personal rather than a business contact.
  'unverified_claim' = Sender claims to have a store but provides no verifiable details — no address and no business contact. Only a store name claim, or only a personal name / store description.
  'no_identity' = No business identity at all. No store name, address, or business contact anywhere.

  HARD RULES:
  - A business name must be a PROPER NAME like 'FreshMart', 'Saigon Home Living', 'ABC Furniture' — not a description.
  - 'a home goods store', 'a furniture store', 'a shop', 'my store', 'I run a store' are descriptions NOT business names.
  - full_identity requires ALL THREE: proper business name + address + contact.
  - When in doubt go LOWER not higher.

---

- order_volume_signal: classify into exactly one of: high_volume, clear_single, small_unstated, no_volume_signal.

  'high_volume' = 2 or more store locations, OR a stated monthly volume above 10 units.
  Signal words: 2 stores, multiple locations, chain, 10+ units a month, container order, ongoing supply.

  'clear_single' = A SINGLE store AND the lead explicitly states a number, quantity, or frequency — e.g. 'around 5 units a month', 'restock every 6 weeks', 'roughly 8 pieces'. Volume must be a countable estimate.
  HARD RULE: vague phrases like 'we order steadily', 'consistent orders', 'we run an established store' do NOT qualify — without a number these are small_unstated.

  'small_unstated' = A single store confirmed but NO number, quantity, or frequency stated anywhere. The lead describes their business but gives no countable volume.

  'no_volume_signal' = No store count and no volume or quantity information at all.

  RULES:
  - A single store only reaches clear_single (14) if a real number is stated. No number = small_unstated (7).
  - When in doubt go LOWER not higher.

---

- product_range_signal: classify into exactly one of: specialist, general_with_furniture, adjacent_category, no_overlap.

  'specialist' = Furniture or home decor specialist retailer. Direct category match.
  Signal words: furniture store, sofa shop, home decor store, homewares retailer, bedroom specialist, interior retail, lifestyle home store.
  HARD RULE: a second-hand, used, vintage, or pre-owned furniture store = adjacent_category NOT specialist.

  'general_with_furniture' = General merchandise retailer that EXPLICITLY includes furniture or home decor in its range.
  RULE: only fires if the retailer explicitly mentions furniture or home products. Default when retailer type is present but not a specialist.

  'adjacent_category' = Related but not directly overlapping — interior design studio, architecture firm, property developer, hotel fit-out, gift shop, boutique, second-hand / vintage / antique furniture.
  RULE: second-hand or used furniture = adjacent_category always.

  'no_overlap' = Completely unrelated category — electronics, mobile phones, clothing, fashion, grocery, supermarket, pharmacy, automotive, sports equipment, restaurant, cafe.
  HARD RULES:
  - Supermarket, grocery, food retailer = no_overlap. No exceptions.
  - Electronics store = no_overlap. No exceptions.
  - 'household goods' alone without explicit furniture = no_overlap.
  - When in doubt go LOWER not higher.

---

- relationship_source_signal: classify into exactly one of: partner_referral, trade_show, outbound_pursuit, unknown_inbound.

  'partner_referral' = Referred by an existing Lumen Living retail partner or known business contact.
  Signal words: referred by, recommended by, your partner, told by your distributor, an existing client suggested.

  'trade_show' = Met Lumen Living at a trade show, furniture expo, or industry exhibition.
  Signal words: trade show, furniture expo, industry fair, we met at, your booth.

  'outbound_pursuit' = Lumen Living initiated cold outreach to this lead. Only use if the message clearly indicates Lumen Living reached out first.

  'unknown_inbound' = Inbound from an unknown or unattributed source. The lead found you online, via search, or gives no relationship context. Default when no other key clearly applies.

  RULES:
  - trade_show requires explicit mention of an event.
  - 'found you online', 'via Google', 'on LinkedIn', 'on your website' = unknown_inbound.
  - Default to unknown_inbound if no relationship signal is present.

---

- price_shopping: true if the retailer explicitly compares wholesale prices across multiple suppliers. false otherwise.

---

GENERAL RULES:
- Return only the JSON object. No markdown. No explanations.
- Only use values from the controlled vocabulary listed above.
- Conservative classification always — when choosing between two levels pick the lower one.
- Never upgrade based on assumptions.
- Only classify what is directly and explicitly stated.

Sender name: {{$json.from_name}}
Sender email: {{$json.from_email}}
Message subject: {{$json.subject}}
Message body: {{$json.body}}"
    }
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 400,
  "seed": 0,
  "top_p": 1
}

nodes.name: Map K Fields

nodes.name: Map Consumer Fields
nodes.notes: Maps the parsed Consumer fields into the standardised lead record format for Supabase. Sets the title with [Consumer] prefix, consumer-specific fields (product_requested, purchase_intent_signal, etc.), review_status to 'Pending', and path to 'consumer'.

nodes.name: Map Retail Fields

nodes.name: Prep for Supabase
nodes.notes: Final data preparation before database insert. Converts string values to proper types: team_size and store_count to integers, stated_revenue_aud to bigint, fields_inferred to integer, price_shopping and cannot_influence to booleans. Adds created_at timestamp. Shared by all three paths (K, Consumer, Retail).

nodes.name: Insert Lead to Supabase
nodes.notes: Inserts the prepared lead record into the crm_leads table using auto-mapped input data. The Supabase database trigger (score_crm_lead) fires automatically on insert, computing the score, confidence_level, tier, recommended_action, attribute_scores, tp_flags, raw_score, and penalty_total fields.

nodes.name: Read Scored Row from Supabase
nodes.notes: Reads back the lead record after insert to get the computed scoring fields. The Supabase trigger (score_crm_lead) runs on INSERT and populates: score, confidence_level, tier, recommended_action, attribute_scores, tp_flags, raw_score, penalty_total. These values are needed for the LLM reason generation and Twenty task creation.

nodes.name: LLM Generate Reasons
nodes.notes: Calls Cerebras LLM to generate exactly 3 top reasons explaining the lead's score. Uses the ICP attribute weights and the Supabase-computed attribute_scores to identify the most impactful factors. Each reason includes: attribute name, earned/max scores, pass/partial/warn icon, and a short explanation under 12 words. Supports all three paths (K, Consumer, Retail) with different attribute sets.

nodes.name: Parse Reasons
nodes.notes: Parses the LLM-generated top_reasons response. Validates it's a 3-item JSON array with correct structure. If the LLM output is malformed, falls back to a deterministic reason generator that uses the attribute_scores directly — picks the 3 highest-scoring attributes and any zero-score attributes with max >= 15. Merges reasons with the full lead record from the scored row.

nodes.name: Update Reasons in Supabase
nodes.notes: Writes the LLM-generated (or fallback) top_reasons JSON array back to the crm_leads record. This is the only field updated after the initial insert — all scoring fields (score, tier, attribute_scores, etc.) were set by the database trigger and remain untouched.

nodes.name: Create Twenty Task
nodes.notes: Creates a task in Twenty CRM (YOUR_TWENTY_HOST) via REST API. Sends the pre-built JSON body containing: title with lead_id for sync matching, markdown note with full score breakdown, and all custom field values (senderName, senderEmail, companyName, leadScore, leadConfidence, recommendation, budgetSignal, timelineSignal, teamSize, urgency, useCase, reviewerNote). Uses allowUnauthorizedCerts for SSL.

nodes.name: Parse Top Reasons
nodes.notes: Ensures top_reasons is a parsed array (not a JSON string) before passing to the task creation node. If top_reasons was stored as a string in Supabase, it parses it back into an array. Passes through all other lead fields unchanged.

nodes.name: Code in JavaScript
nodes.notes: Builds the Twenty task payload. Formats the title with path label, sender name, score, email, and lead_id. Constructs the markdown note body with score summary, top reasons with icons, attribute score breakdown, and TP flags. Maps all lead fields to Twenty custom field names (senderName, leadScore, etc.). Pre-builds the entire JSON body using JSON.stringify() to prevent control character issues in the HTTP Request node.

nodes.name: Prepare Field List
nodes.notes: One-time setup node. Takes the Task object ID from the metadata query and generates a list of GraphQL mutations to create each custom field (12 TEXT fields + 1 SELECT field for reviewDecision). Each item in the output becomes a separate API call in the Create Twenty Field node. Part of the setup flow triggered by 'Run Setup Once'.

nodes.name: Get Task Object ID

parameters.jsCode:
const inputData = $input.first().json;
const leadData = inputData?.leadData || {};
const context = inputData?.context || '';

function cleanText(text) {
return (text || '')
.split('\n')
.filter(line => !line.trim().startsWith('>'))
.join(' ')
.replace(/[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x7F]/g, '')
.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
.trim()
.substring(0, 500);
}

const historyText = cleanText(inputData?.historyText || '');
const latestMessage = cleanText(leadData?.email_body || '');
const cleanContext = cleanText(context);

const prompt = `You are a sales assistant for Lumen Living, a luxury Vietnamese furniture brand.

Write a helpful reply email to the customer's LATEST message below.

Use the conversation history only to understand context.
Use ONLY the product information provided in the Product context.
Never make up prices, dimensions, lead times, finishes, stock status, delivery details, discounts, or commercial terms.

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULE:

* Return the email body only.
* Do NOT return JSON.
* Do NOT include a subject line.
* Do NOT include explanations about what you are doing.

LANGUAGE RULE:

* Reply in the same language as the detected_language field below.

EMAIL FORMAT RULES:

* Start with: Hi [Customer Name],
* Do NOT start with Dear.
* Use short paragraphs with blank lines between sections.
* Do NOT write the whole reply as one long paragraph.
* Do NOT hard-wrap sentences across multiple lines.
* Use bullet points only when listing multiple finishes, product options, or grouped product details.
* End exactly with:
  Kind regards,
  Lumen Living Team

CONTENT RULES:

* Thank the customer for their interest.
* Address every product the customer asked about by name.
* Never mention products the customer did not ask about.
* Do NOT repeat the same fact twice.
* If price is available and allowed by the pricing rules, mention it once before Product details.
* If dimensions, lead time, delivery location, or preferred delivery time are included, put them only under "Product details:" as bullet points.
* If a requested finish or colour is unavailable but alternatives are available, explain this clearly in one paragraph.
* If there are multiple available finishes, list them as bullet points.
* If required information is missing, politely ask the customer to confirm it.
* Do NOT mention CRM, score, tier, lead quality, internal routing, attribute scores, TP flags, or penalties.

PRICING RULES — CRITICAL:

* Customer path: ${leadData.path}
* If path = 'consumer' → show RETAIL price only. Never mention B2B price, trade price, wholesale price, dealer price, or any discount.
* If path = 'retail' → NEVER show retail price. ONLY quote B2B trade price if available in the context. End by directing them to na.lumenliving.com/pages/b2b-signup.

PREFERRED STRUCTURE FOR CONSUMER:
Hi [Customer Name],

Thank you for your interest in [Product Name]. The retail price for this piece is [Retail Price].

Please note that [Unavailable Finish] is currently unavailable. However, we do have [Product Name] available in the following finishes:

* [Available finish 1]
* [Available finish 2]

Product details:

* Dimensions: [Dimensions]
* Estimated lead time: [Estimated lead time]
* Delivery location: [Delivery location]
* Preferred delivery time: [Preferred delivery time]

Please let us know if you would like to proceed, and we will be happy to confirm the next steps for you.

Kind regards,
Lumen Living Team

PREFERRED STRUCTURE FOR RETAIL:
Hi [Customer Name],

Thank you for your enquiry about [Product Name]. We would be happy to assist with your trade or B2B request.

[Quote B2B trade price only if available. If not available, say we can confirm trade pricing after receiving the required business details.]

Product details:

* Dimensions: [Dimensions]
* Estimated lead time: [Estimated lead time]
* Available finishes: [Available finishes]

To continue with a trade enquiry, please complete the B2B signup form here: na.lumenliving.com/pages/b2b-signup

Kind regards,
Lumen Living Team

IMPORTANT:

* Follow the correct preferred structure based on the customer path.
* Only include information that exists in the Product context.
* Do not include placeholder text such as [Retail Price], [Dimensions], or [Available finish].
* If a section has no available information, omit that section.
* Keep "Product details:" as a separate section if product details exist.
* Keep bullet points on separate lines.

Customer name: ${leadData.sender_name || ''}
Detected language: ${leadData.detected_language || 'en'}
Customer path: ${leadData.path || ''}
Customer city: ${leadData.extracted_city || ''}
Customer district: ${leadData.extracted_district || ''}

Conversation history:
${historyText || 'No previous conversation — this is the first message.'}

Customer's latest message:
${latestMessage}

Product context:
${cleanContext}`;

const response = await this.helpers.httpRequest({
method: 'POST',
url: 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions',
headers: {
'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.GROQ_API_KEY,
'Content-Type': 'application/json'
},
body: {
model: 'llama-3.3-70b-versatile',
stream: false,
temperature: 0.2,
max_tokens: 700,
seed: 0,
top_p: 1,
messages: [
{
role: 'user',
content: prompt
}
]
},
json: true
});

return [{ json: {
...inputData,
choices: response?.choices
}}];
